## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, open sets $U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$, a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $T : U \to V$, and a nonnegative Lebesgue measurable function $f : V \to [0,\infty]$.

[L1] The formula already holds for continuous compactly supported integrands. ([[lem-c-one-change-of-variables-for-continuous-compactly-supported-integrands]])

[L2] Monotone convergence passes increasing limits through the integral. ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]])

[L3] Every nonnegative measurable function admits increasing simple approximations. ([[thm-nonnegative-measurable-functions-admit-increasing-simple-approximations]])

[L4] Assuming countable choice, Lebesgue measurable sets are Borel up to null sets, and $T$ preserves both null sets and Lebesgue measurability. ([[cor-lebesgue-sigma-algebra-is-the-completion-of-borel-lebesgue-measure]], [[lem-c-one-diffeomorphisms-map-lebesgue-null-sets-to-null-sets]], [[lem-c-one-diffeomorphisms-map-lebesgue-measurable-sets-to-lebesgue-measurable-sets]])

[L5] Two measures on $V$ agreeing on a generating pi-system with a common increasing finite-mass exhaustion from that system agree on all Borel sets ([[thm-measure-uniqueness-on-a-sigma-finite-pi-system]]).

[L6] The nonnegative integral is additive ([[cor-additivity-of-the-nonnegative-lebesgue-integral]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 On Borel subsets $E$ of $V$ define $$\nu(E):=\int_U\mathbf1_E(T(x))|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x).$$ This is a measure: the nonnegative Jacobian weight is measurable, inverse images under $T$ take disjoint countable unions to disjoint countable unions, [L6] gives finite additivity, and [L2] passes the increasing finite sums through the integral. [L2, L6, given]

2.1 Let $W=V\cap R$ for a bounded open rectangle $R$ with rational endpoints. Write $d(y,W^c)$ for Euclidean distance to the complement and $\|y\|_\infty$ for the maximum coordinate modulus. The functions $$\varphi_j(y)=\min\{1,\max(0,jd(y,W^c)-1)\}\min\{1,\max(0,j+1-\|y\|_\infty)\}$$ are continuous, nonnegative and increase pointwise to $\mathbf1_W$. Each support is contained in the compact set $\{d(y,W^c)\ge1/j,\ \|y\|_\infty\le j+1\}\subset W$, so $\varphi_j|_V$ has compact support in $V$. Applying [L1] to each $\varphi_j$ and [L2] to the two monotone limits gives $\nu(W)=\lambda_n(W)$. The empty $W$ is immediate. [L1, L2, step 1.1]

3.1 The sets $V\cap R$ above form a pi-system generating the Borel sigma-algebra of $V$. The increasing members $P_j=V\cap(-j,j)^n$ cover $V$ and satisfy $\lambda_n(P_j)<\infty$; step 2.1 gives $\nu(P_j)=\lambda_n(P_j)$. Hence [L5] makes $\nu(E)=\lambda_n(E)$ for every Borel $E\subseteq V$. This proves the set formula without assuming that an infinite-measure equality class is closed under decreasing intersections. [L5, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 Let $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j \mathbf 1_{E_j}$ be a nonnegative simple Lebesgue measurable function. By [L4], replace each $E_j$ by a Borel set differing from it only by a null set. The set formula from step 3.1 and null-set invariance in [L4] then give the change-of-variables formula for $s$. [L2, L4, step 3.1]

5.1 Choose simple functions $s_k \uparrow f$ by [L3]. Step 4.1 applies to each $s_k$, and [L2] lets $k \to \infty$ on both sides. This yields the formula for $f$. [L2, L3, step 4.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $P=(P_1,\ldots,P_k)$ have the Dirichlet distribution with
positive parameters $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$. If
$I_1,\ldots,I_r$ is a partition of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ into nonempty groups,
then
$$\left(\sum_{j\in I_1}P_j,\ldots,\sum_{j\in I_r}P_j\right)\sim\operatorname{Dirichlet}(b_1,\ldots,b_r),\qquad b_\ell=\sum_{j\in I_\ell}a_j.$$
When $r=1$, the grouped vector is the point mass at $1$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC; positive $a_1,\ldots,a_k$; and a partition of the coordinate indices into nonempty groups.

[A1] Full AC is assumed. [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

[A2] Full AC implies the Countable Choice required by Gamma density normalization. [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]] [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] On a finite discrete standard Borel space, the normalized-gamma construction realizes a positive-parameter Dirichlet vector as independent $\operatorname{Gamma}(a_j,1)$ increments divided by their sum. [[thm-existence-of-dirichlet-process-by-normalized-gamma-poisson-random-measure]].

[F2] Under Countable Choice, a shape-rate Gamma$(a,1)$ variable has density $z^{a-1}e^{-z}/\Gamma(a)$, normalized for $a>0$; the Euler Gamma value is finite and positive. [[def-gamma-distribution-shape-rate]] [[def-real-gamma-function-by-the-euler-integral]] [[thm-real-gamma-euler-integral-convergence]].

[F3] Under Countable Choice, the nonnegative Lebesgue change-of-variables formula holds for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms. [[thm-c-one-change-of-variables-for-nonnegative-lebesgue-measurable-functions]].

[F4] Finite measures with an exponential moment and the same Laplace transform on a neighborhood of zero are equal under AC. [[lem-uniqueness-of-a-multivariate-exponential-transform]].

[F5] Finite products of probability measures exist and satisfy the rectangle product formula. [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]].

[F6] The finite-dimensional Dirichlet law is the positive-parameter simplex law specified in [[def-dirichlet-distribution]].

## Proof

**Given:** The hypotheses in the Statement.

1.1 Apply [F1] to the finite discrete space $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ with base masses $a_j$. Thus the law of $P$ is that of $Z_j/\sum_{h=1}^kZ_h$, where the $Z_j$ are independent $\operatorname{Gamma}(a_j,1)$ variables, and it is the Dirichlet law [F6]. [A1, F1, F5, F6, given, construct]

2.1 For $u<1$, [F2] and the change of variables $t=(1-u)z$ in [F3] give $\mathbb E e^{uZ_j}=\Gamma(a_j)^{-1}\int_0^\infty z^{a_j-1}e^{-(1-u)z}dz=(1-u)^{-a_j}$. For $W_\ell=\sum_{j\in I_\ell}Z_j$, independence therefore gives the joint moment-generating function $\prod_{\ell=1}^r(1-u_\ell)^{-b_\ell}$ for $|u_\ell|<\delta<1$, since the groups use disjoint coordinates in the finite product law [F5]. [A1, A2, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F5], the product law of independent $\operatorname{Gamma}(b_\ell,1)$ variables exists and has the same joint transform. Both laws have finite exponential moment at every $0<\delta<1$, since the transform at $(\delta,\ldots,\delta)$ is finite. Applying [F4] to the difference of these two finite measures shows that $(W_1,\ldots,W_r)$ has that product Gamma law. [A1, A2, F4, F5, step 2.1]

4.1 Normalize the grouped variables by their common positive total. The resulting vector is Dirichlet with parameters $(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ by [F1], while $W_\ell/\sum_hW_h=\sum_{j\in I_\ell}P_j$ by step 1.1. This proves the claim for $r\ge2$. For $r=1$ the only coordinate sum is $\sum_{j=1}^kP_j=1$, which is the stated one-category law. [F1, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra, cases] ∎

Applying [F4] to the difference of these two finite measures shows that $(W_1,\ldots,W_r)$ has that product Gamma law.

The resulting vector is Dirichlet with parameters $(b_1,\ldots,b_r)$ by [F1], while $W_\ell/\sum_hW_h=\sum_{j\in I_\ell}P_j$ by step 1.1. This proves the claim for $r\ge2$. For $r=1$ the only coordinate sum is $\sum_{j=1}^kP_j=1$, which is the stated one-category law.

## Example

Assume AC. Let $\mathsf X=\{a,b\}$ with the discrete sigma-algebra and let
$\alpha=\delta_a$, so $\alpha(\{b\})=0$. In the model
$G\sim DP(\alpha)$ and $X_1\mid G\sim G$, examine the data event
$\{X_1=b\}$.

Separately, let $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal B)$ be any standard Borel space, let
$\gamma$ be a finite nonzero diffuse measure (meaning
$\gamma(\{z\})=0$ for every $z\in\mathsf Y$), and fix one $y\in\mathsf Y$.
The verification also checks the posterior-version freedom on this fixed
singleton data fiber.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite space and base measure in the Example.

[A1] Assume AC, as required by the process existence and posterior results. [[def-axiom-of-choice]].

[F1] A cell with zero base mass has $G$-mass zero almost surely under $DP(\alpha)$. [[def-dirichlet-process]] [[thm-existence-of-dirichlet-process-by-normalized-gamma-poisson-random-measure]].

[F2] For every finite nonzero base measure, the normalized-Gamma theorem defines $DP$ and the posterior update gives the measurable kernel $z\mapsto DP(\gamma+\delta_z)$ satisfying disintegration. [[thm-existence-of-dirichlet-process-by-normalized-gamma-poisson-random-measure]] [[thm-dirichlet-process-posterior-update]] [[def-bayesian-posterior-as-regular-conditional-law]].

[F3] In a one-draw model with finite nonzero base measure $\beta$, $\Pr(X_1\in A)=\beta(A)/\beta(\mathsf X)$. [[thm-dirichlet-process-polya-urn-predictive-law]].

[F4] In a standard Borel space every singleton is measurable: under a Polish presentation it corresponds to a closed singleton. [[def-standard-borel-space]].

[F5] A probability kernel has probability-measure sections and measurable evaluations; its disintegration identity is checked on measurable rectangles. [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]] [[def-probability-measure]] [[def-bayesian-posterior-as-regular-conditional-law]].

## Verification

**Given:** The finite two-point model in the Example and, separately, the standard Borel diffuse-base model $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal B,\gamma)$ with fixed $y\in\mathsf Y$.

1.1 By [F1], $G(\{b\})=0$ almost surely. Since $\Pr(X_1=b\mid G)=G(\{b\})$, integration over the prior gives $\Pr(X_1=b)=0$, also agreeing with [F3]. [A1, F1, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 The formula in [F2] assigns $K(b)=DP(\delta_a+\delta_b)$ at the null data value. Define another kernel by $K'(a)=K(a)$ and $K'(b)=DP(\delta_a)$. Both sections are probability measures, and $K'$ is measurable because $\{b\}$ is measurable in the discrete data space. For any measurable event $C$ in $\mathcal P(\mathsf X)$, the disintegration integrals for $K$ and $K'$ differ only at $b$, which has data-marginal mass zero by step 1.1. Thus both are posterior versions; the update formula at $b$ is a version choice, not evidence-supported learning. [F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 In the separate diffuse-base model, [F3] gives data-marginal mass $M(\{y\})=\gamma(\{y\})/\gamma(\mathsf Y)=0$. Let $K(z)=DP(\gamma+\delta_z)$ be the posterior kernel from [F2] and set $K'(z)=K(z)$ for $z\ne y$, $K'(y)=DP(\gamma)$. By [F4], $\{y\}$ is measurable. For every measurable $C\subseteq\mathcal P(\mathsf Y)$, $z\mapsto K'(z,C)=\mathbf1_{\mathsf Y\setminus\{y\}}(z)K(z,C)+\mathbf1_{\{y\}}(z)DP(\gamma)(C)$ is measurable; each section is a probability measure, so [F5] makes $K'$ a probability kernel. The disintegration integrals for $K$ and $K'$ agree on every measurable rectangle because the kernels differ only on $\{y\}$ and $M(\{y\})=0$. Thus $K'$ is also a posterior version, proving that the displayed update value at this fixed null fiber is not uniquely determined. [F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra, construct] ∎
